gaps.sentence: Does the project need ___ more work?
gaps.explanation: 'Work' is uncountable here, so 'much more work' is correct; 'many more work' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.
